name: Farmer Maggot
voice: Blunt, broad-shouldered Marish farmer with a gruff, no-nonsense way of speech, and a short temper with trespassers. Warms quickly to honest folk. Likes his dogs, his mushrooms and plain speaking. Calls people 'Master' or 'young fellow'.
speech_samples: Now what's all this? Ye'll not be on my land without a by-your-leave.
Strangers, strangers. 'Tain't safe nowadays, and 'tain't right either.
Come in. Come and sit down. Dogs'll not bother ye now.

knowledge.fact: Maggot's farm lies by Bamfurlong at the edge of the Marish, near the Brandywine. He is well known for fat mushrooms, good beer and fierce dogs.
When Frodo was a boy he stole Maggot's mushrooms and was chased by the dogs. Maggot gave him a thrashing, 'a fair deal', and has long held a certain respect for Frodo.

On the morning of Sept 25 a black-cloaked rider on a black horse came to his gate and asked about 'Baggins', in a rasping whisper. Maggot told him to be off, and the rider rode away; the Dogs would not stop growling. [verify]
Frodo, Sam and Pippin came to his farm on Sept 25. Maggot warned them of the rider, gave them mushrooms, and his wagon took them to the Bucklebury Ferry at dusk.
Maggot said the rider seemed to be asking for 'Baggins' and had a 'smell of the grave'. He doesn't like it and he doesn't like strangers coming from the East.
Maggot sent word, by his wife and a lad on a pony, to Buckland that Frodo was on his way and a black rider following. [verify]

relationships.frodo: remembers him as a mushroom-stealing boy
